trainers.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions about Sadiq’s experiment.

atoms.text: Sadiq wants to measure the frequency of the sounds produced by his home-made guitar. To build it, he used elastic bands of different thicknesses and an empty butter tub.

atoms.a: What should stay the same about the elastic bands to make it a fair test?

correct.text: By keeping the length of the bands the same, the tightness of the bands around the butter tub can’t have an effect on Sadiq’s results.

wrong.text: Not quite. The colour of the elastic bands won’t have any effect on the results.

atoms.a: What should Sadiq use to measure the frequency of the sounds made when he plucks the strings?

feedback.end: By using a frequency counter, Sadiq will be able to record precise, reliable data. This will make his results easier to compare and also help to make his experiment a fair test.

instruction.text: Choose the correct words to fill the gaps in Sadiq’s hypothesis.

atoms.sound: I think the wider the elastic band I pluck, the lower the pitch of the sound will be.

instruction.text: Sadiq plucks each band with the same amount of force. Record the values of each frequency counter in the table below.

trainers.layout:
a1 b1
a2 b2
a3 b3
a4 b4
trainers.hint: Hz represents the unit hertz, which is used to measure frequency.

trainers.instruction: Which elastic band produced the lowest-pitched sound?
trainers.hint: The lower the frequency, the lower the pitch.

trainers.instruction: Which elastic band was the thickest?
trainers.hint:
High-pitched sounds = small, tight or thin.
Low-pitched sounds = big, loose or thick.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in Sadiq’s conclusion of his experiment.

atoms.b: In the experiment, the ((++results insects)) proved that the wider the elastic band is, the lower the ((++pitch volume)) of the sound produced.
